scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8878: Users in both pods report the "web2.local" portal
returns nothing -- connections fail immediately instead of loading. The other
portals (web0/web1/web3) load fine. DNS resolves web2.local to 10.200.0.5,
and ping to 10.200.0.5 works from user machines. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_2

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: web_server_2 Apache (apache2) HTTP service
Mechanism: the apache2 service on web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) is stopped, so
  nothing listens on TCP/80 and connection attempts are refused immediately.
  Everything below the service layer is healthy: DNS still resolves
  web2.local -> 10.200.0.5, the OSPF path delivers packets (ping succeeds),
  and the other three web servers keep serving. The symptom is purely the
  dead HTTP daemon on one server.
Localization: web_server_2
Root cause: apache2 not running on web_server_2 (TCP/80 closed)
Fix: `service apache2 start` on web_server_2
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_2 (e.g. `service apache2 start`
/ `systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache listens on port 80 again,
http://web2.local serves normally. Nothing else needs changing.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-dns-and-network: notes DNS resolves web2.local correctly and 10.200.0.5 is reachable at the IP layer, ruling out name resolution and the network path

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: the HTTP application service on web_server_2 (10.200.0.5). Mechanism: clients can reach the server IP (ICMP succeeds), but there is no process listening on TCP/80, so SYNs to port 80 are refused immediately (RST), making browsers/curl fail instantly rather than time out. Localization: specific to web_server_2’s application layer; L3/L2 connectivity and routing in the fabric are healthy. Evidence: netstat on web_server_2 shows no 0.0.0.0:80 listener (only 127.0.0.11 ephemeral services), while web_server_0/1/3 each show “0.0.0.0:80 LISTEN.” From a user host, curl to http://10.200.0.5 returns immediately with no connect phase (total ~1.3 ms), consistent with connection refusal. Systemd reports apache2 is loaded/enabled but “inactive (dead)” on web_server_2. Root cause: the web service (apache2) is not running on web_server_2, leaving port 80 closed. Corrective fix: start or restart the HTTP service and ensure it remains enabled. On web_server_2, run: systemctl restart apache2 && systemctl status apache2 to confirm “active (running).” If it fails, check configuration and logs (e.g., /var/log/apache2/error.log) for syntax/bind errors; alternatively, start the intended web daemon (nginx vs apache2) per your build. After restoring the listener, re-validate from user hosts (curl/http) and confirm 0.0.0.0:80 LISTEN appears in netstat.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) as the affected device in multiple places.
Agent explicitly states apache2 on web_server_2 is inactive/not listening on TCP/80 and identifies restarting the service as the fix.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-dns-and-network: notes DNS resolves web2.local correctly and 10.200.0.5 is reachable at the IP layer, ruling out name resolution and the network path
per_axis.rationale: The report confirms IP-layer reachability and healthy L2/L3, but it does not state that DNS (web2.local) resolves correctly to 10.200.0.5.
Proposes restarting/enabling the apache2 service on web_server_2 and verifying it runs, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's log shows interface IPs, a netstat on web_server_2 with no :80 listener, systemctl reporting apache2 inactive (dead), and a quick failed curl from a client — together these directly support the diagnosis that the apache2 daemon is stopped and nothing is listening on TCP/80. The inference and recommended fix follow logically and essential alternative checks (other servers, interface, service status) were performed.
